title: Night Flight
blurb: Finn and Zeb fly to Mars to find a safe spot for the first space base.
cover_prompt: Finn and Zeb in white and orange spacesuits with clear bubble helmets stand heroically on the red surface of Mars in front of their sleek white and orange rocket, a pink sky with two tiny moons and the small blue dot of Earth above, a six-wheeled rover and a cave hill behind them.

sound.label: /igh/
sound.intro: Listen for the /igh/ sound, as in night. In this story it is spelt three ways. Tap a word to hear it.

cracked: Finn and Zeb found two good spots for a base on Mars and sent the plan home.

text: Finn and Zeb are in the Den at night. Ping!
Mars needs a safe spot for a space base.
p1.prompt: Inside the cosy explorer den at night, a big wall screen shows the red planet Mars with a flashing beacon; Finn, in his explorer outfit, salutes the screen while Zeb holds up a toy rocket, both excited.

text: Finn is the pilot. Zeb sits by his side.
Five, four, three, two, one... lift off!
p2.prompt: Inside a bright rocket cockpit, Finn in a white and orange spacesuit sits in the pilot seat gripping the controls, Zeb in a matching small spacesuit beside him pressing a big red button; through the window flames and smoke as the rocket lifts off.

text: The ship zooms high into the night sky.
Mars is a tiny red dot. It gets bigger.
p3.prompt: A sleek white and orange rocket ship zooms through a deep blue night sky full of stars, Earth small behind it, Mars a glowing red dot ahead growing bigger; Finn and Zeb visible through the cockpit window pointing ahead.

text: They land on wide, dry, red land.
The sky is pink! Zeb jumps up high.
p4.prompt: Finn and Zeb in white and orange spacesuits with clear bubble helmets stand on wide dry red Martian ground under a pale pink sky beside their landed rocket; Zeb is mid-air in a huge joyful jump, Finn laughing with arms up.

text: Stop one: a cave in the side of a hill.
Finn shines a light. It is dry inside.
p5.prompt: Finn and Zeb in spacesuits stand at the mouth of a big dark cave in the side of a red Martian hill; Finn shines a torch beam into the dry rocky cave, Zeb peeks around him. A small six-wheeled rover is parked outside.

text: In the cave, a base can hide from the
hot sun rays. But it is dark all the time.
p6.prompt: Inside the red Martian cave, Finn holds up a glowing tablet showing a sketch of a little dome base inside the cave; Zeb holds the torch. Outside the cave mouth the sun blazes with bright rays while the cave is cool and dark.

text: Stop two: the ice at the top of Mars.
It is white and bright! Zeb slides on it.
p7.prompt: Finn and Zeb in spacesuits at the bright white icy north pole of Mars under a pink sky; Zeb slides on his tummy across the ice with a huge grin, Finn claps, the rover parked nearby on the red and white ground.

text: Ice can melt into water to drink.
But at night it is colder than a freezer.
p8.prompt: Finn in a spacesuit kneels on the Martian ice holding up a clear flask with a chunk of ice melting into water; Zeb shivers dramatically with a frosty helmet; the sun is low and the sky turning dark blue with stars.

text: A dust devil spins by! Quick!
Which way, Finn?
c1.prompt: On the red Martian plain a tall swirling dust devil whirls towards Finn and Zeb in their spacesuits; to one side is a big boulder, to the other side the six-wheeled rover with its door open. Finn points both ways, Zeb clutches his helmet.

text: They hide behind a big rock. Dust zips by.
Zeb's helmet is red now! Nice, says Zeb.
b1a.prompt: Finn and Zeb crouch behind a big red boulder as a dust devil whirls past, red dust streaming by; Zeb's bubble helmet is coated in red dust and he grins through it, Finn gives a thumbs up.

text: They jump in the rover. It rocks side
to side. Then the sky is pink again. Phew!
b1b.prompt: Finn and Zeb inside the cabin of the six-wheeled rover holding on tight as it rocks, red dust swirling against the windows; through the front window the dust devil is moving away and pink sky returning.

text: Finn must pick a spot for the base.
Which is best? Think, then decide!

reveal.text: Space scientists have the same big question. Some like caves and lava tubes, because the rock shields a base from the sun's rays. Some like the ice, because ice means water. Nobody has picked yet!

c2.prompt: Finn and Zeb in spacesuits stand on a Martian ridge looking at a big floating holographic map of Mars showing a cave on a hill on one side and a white ice cap on the other, with a glowing question mark in the middle; Finn rubs his chin, Zeb points at the ice.

text: The cave it is! A rover can fetch ice.
The base will hide from the rays all day.
b2a.prompt: Imagined Martian base: a cosy glowing dome tucked inside the red cave, warm lights in its windows, the six-wheeled rover driving back with blocks of ice; Finn and Zeb in spacesuits in the foreground, Finn holding the plan, Zeb cheering.

text: The ice it is! Lots of water to drink.
They will pile up thick white walls.
b2b.prompt: Imagined Martian base on the white ice cap under a pink sky: a dome with thick white ice-block walls and a glowing door, a water tank beside it; Finn and Zeb in spacesuits stack a big block of ice together, grinning.

text: Right in the middle! Not far from the ice,
not far from the cave. Finn likes it.
b2c.prompt: Imagined Martian base: a dome on an open red plain halfway between a cave hill on the left and a white ice cap on the right, with rover tracks running both ways; Finn and Zeb in spacesuits stand proudly in front, Finn holding up the plan.

text: Finn sends the plan to Mars Control.
Nice job, Finn and Zeb! says the voice.
p9.prompt: Inside the rocket cockpit, Finn in a spacesuit without his helmet taps a glowing screen showing the base plan with a big green tick and a radio wave symbol; Zeb hugs a toy rocket, both smiling, Mars red through the window.

text: Time to fly home. But Zeb wants to see
the two tiny moons first. Which way?
c3.prompt: Finn and Zeb in spacesuits stand by their rocket on the red Martian plain at dusk; in the darkening pink sky two tiny lumpy moons are just visible, and far off a small blue dot that is Earth; Zeb points up at the moons, Finn points at the rocket door.

text: They lift off into the pink sky.
Earth is a bright blue dot. Home!
b3a.prompt: The white and orange rocket lifts off from Mars into a pink and purple sky, Finn and Zeb waving through the cockpit window; far ahead in the dark starry space a small bright blue dot, Earth.

text: Two tiny moons shine in the sky.
One is like a potato! Then they fly home.
b3b.prompt: Finn and Zeb in spacesuits gaze up at two small lumpy grey moons shining in the dark Martian sky, one shaped just like a potato; Zeb giggles pointing at it, Finn looks through a small telescope. The rocket waits behind them.

text: Back in the Den that night, Finn pins up
the plan. A base on Mars! Case cracked!
p10.prompt: Back in the cosy explorer den, Finn pins a drawing of a dome base on Mars onto the corkboard of case notes while Zeb zooms a toy rocket through the air; the wall screen shows Mars with a big green tick.

casefile.title: Mars
casefile.subtitle: The red planet, next door to Earth.

facts.text: A day on Mars is about 40 minutes longer than a day on Earth.
Mars has two tiny moons, Phobos and Deimos. Phobos is 26 km across, about a half-hour car trip.
Olympus Mons on Mars is the biggest volcano we know. It is 27 km high, three times taller than Mount Everest.

casefile.prompt: A Creature Cases style fact file portrait of the planet Mars: a red dusty landscape with a cave hill, a white ice cap, the giant volcano Olympus Mons on the horizon, a small six-wheeled rover, and two tiny lumpy moons in a pink sky; clean, bright, centred, like a collector card illustration, no text.

quiz.why: A cave in the side of a hill.

quiz.q: What is at the top of Mars?
quiz.why: White, bright ice. Zeb slid on it.

quiz.q: Why is the cave a good spot for a base?

options.text: It hides from the sun's rays

quiz.why: The rock keeps the hot rays out.

quiz.q: Why would a base need the ice?

options.text: Ice can melt into water to drink
Ice is fun to slide on

debrief.question: Would you rather live in the cave or by the ice? Why?
